scope: Change detection, portfolio risk, probabilistic modeling and formal/concurrency testing
method: Pinned official repository source/document review, including README and license inspection, with commit identifiers recorded. Findings are research notes, not an endorsement or runtime integration approval. No REA execution or SYLPH runtime tests were performed in this batch.

provenance: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit ee1c8ff8a548d54c641b2bb471562165931f31c7 (master); accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Python library for offline change-point detection in non-stationary signals, with exact and approximate parametric/nonparametric algorithms.
The documented example fits a PELT model to a supplied signal and predicts breakpoints; this is retrospective segmentation, not a live alert guarantee.
patterns: Run regime segmentation over timestamped, point-in-time feature series and persist algorithm, cost model, penalty, and fit window.
Keep change-point output labeled as offline research evidence.
overlap: Existing feed freshness and divergence checks already monitor operational state; ruptures would add offline statistical analysis only.
risks: Retrospective breakpoint detection can leak future observations into training.
Python library should not become a runtime dependency without latency, operational, and reproducibility review.
validation: Use chronological splits and synthetic regime-shift fixtures.
Assert all feature windows end at the decision timestamp and tune thresholds only on training folds.
evidence: Official repository README and LICENSE inspected at pinned commit ee1c8ff8a548d54c641b2bb471562165931f31c7 (master); accessed 2026-10-14.

discoveries: Python portfolio analytics toolkit provides performance statistics, plots, reports/tearsheets, and Monte Carlo analysis.
Its metrics operate on supplied return series; correct fills, cash flows, fees, and valuation marks are prerequisites for meaningful results.
patterns: Calculate risk-adjusted and drawdown metrics from reconciled net returns.
Keep analytics output separate from trade authorization; preserve the exact return-series provenance and open-position valuation policy.
overlap: No need to duplicate the execution ledger; use its verified fill/fee records as analytical inputs.
risks: Bad, incomplete, or survivorship-biased return series create misleading performance claims.
Python implementation is not a direct TypeScript engine integration.
validation: Cross-check metrics against hand-calculated deterministic return series.
Include failed transactions, fees, transfers, and open-position valuation policy.

validation: Compare against simple baselines with walk-forward evaluation.

provenance: Official README and root LICENSE inspected at pinned commit c2fd0e05c648d353467bdb15fd6149a103b3a981 (master); accessed 2026-10-14. LICENSE identifies Alibi Detect as Business Source License 1.1, with a four-year change license to Apache-2.0 and restrictions on commercial production use.
discoveries: Source-available Python package for outlier, adversarial, and data/concept drift detection, supporting online and offline detectors across tabular, text, image, and time-series data.
README lists statistical and learned drift detectors, including KS, MMD, and classifier-based approaches.
The pinned root license is BUSL-1.1, not permissive MPL; production/commercial use has restrictions unless separately licensed or the change date applies.
patterns: Track feature-distribution drift against versioned reference cohorts; record detector, backend, reference data, threshold, and score.
Emit advisory monitoring signals with detector version and threshold; do not equate drift with an actionable market signal.
overlap: Existing runtime divergence checks cover operational comparisons; statistical drift analysis is complementary and should not duplicate their authority.
risks: Drift is not proof of model failure or a market opportunity; reference cohorts and thresholds can cause false alarms or missed shifts.
The current license restricts commercial production usage; do not adopt for a commercial SYLPH service without legal review/appropriate license.
Optional TensorFlow/PyTorch/KeOps backends add substantial dependency and reproducibility considerations.
validation: Test known synthetic shifts and stable controls.
Measure false positives and detection delay on chronological holdouts.
Confirm license and backend terms before any deployment.

overlap: Complements deterministic TypeScript regression tests; does not replace them.
risks: Model assumptions and bounds can omit implementation details; passing a model does not prove deployed code conforms.

validation: Review model-to-code correspondence and preserve counterexamples.
Add executable regression tests for discovered counterexamples; record model bounds and configuration.

provenance: Official README and repository license metadata inspected at pinned commit 9a13950e0ebddcb3d7a79cb9e854b0866e1c5712 (main); accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Apalache is a symbolic model checker for TLA+ and Quint that translates specifications into constraints for SMT solvers such as Z3 and CVC5.
Documentation distinguishes inductive invariant checking from bounded execution safety checking, with parameter/bound assumptions.
patterns: Check bounded invariants for retry, checkpoint, queue-capacity, and live-tail handoff state machines.
Version control model configuration and counterexample traces; treat bounds as part of reported evidence.
overlap: Formal exploration supplements runtime tests without entering the trading process.
risks: Bounded verification cannot establish behavior outside the modeled bounds.
Specification drift can make a passing model irrelevant; using an SMT solver does not prove the implementation itself.
validation: Validate specification variables and transitions against current implementation.
Turn meaningful counterexamples into deterministic regression cases and explicitly report bounds.

patterns: Check arithmetic invariants for fee and position accounting in an offline verification harness.

risks: Incorrect encodings or omitted constraints yield irrelevant assurance.

The repository explicitly targets Python and does not analyze SYLPH TypeScript directly.
patterns: Apply contract-based symbolic checks to isolated Python research utilities, if present.
Use explicit preconditions/postconditions as a design pattern for typed runtime APIs.
sylphModules: offline historical data tooling, if Python is introduced

risks: Python-only analysis must not be represented as verification of the TypeScript runtime.

validation: Restrict conclusions to analyzed Python functions and pinned tool configuration.
Test equivalent TypeScript behavior with the project test stack.

discoveries: Proptest is a Rust property-testing framework in the QuickCheck/Hypothesis family.
Generated failures can be reduced to smaller counterexamples and test-case persistence supports reproducibility.
A Rust property-testing harness does not exercise SYLPH TypeScript unless a Rust component is the actual subject.
patterns: Generate slot-order permutations, duplicate deliveries, and malformed inputs in the language-native property test harness.
Persist minimized counterexamples as regression fixtures and record seeds/configuration.
overlap: Use current TypeScript test stack for implementation tests; consider Rust tool only for Rust components.
risks: A Rust test harness does not establish TypeScript runtime correctness.
Randomized tests without stored seeds and minimized cases can be difficult to reproduce.
validation: Port relevant invariants to SYLPH’s TypeScript test framework.
Record seeds and retain shrunk counterexamples.

discoveries: Loom is a concurrency permutation-testing tool for Rust using instrumented synchronization primitives.
Its target is Rust synchronization and memory-ordering behavior, not JavaScript event-loop semantics.
patterns: Enumerate race-sensitive transition orders if SYLPH adds a Rust concurrent component.
Translate relevant ordering scenarios into deterministic scheduler-controlled TypeScript tests.
overlap: No direct dependency for the current TypeScript engine.
risks: Applying Rust model-check results to JavaScript behavior is invalid.
Instrumentation and explored schedules do not cover every possible real execution.
validation: Use Loom only for Rust components actually under test.
For TypeScript, inject scheduler/order controls and assert state transitions directly.

discoveries: Jepsen is a Clojure framework for running operations against a distributed system, injecting faults, recording histories, and checking those histories for correctness.
A test requires a concrete system adapter, workload, fault model, and checker; its run artifacts include operation history and analysis.
The README warns that tests can alter clocks, firewall rules, and processes, and says not to run them against production systems.
patterns: Design isolated fault scenarios for stream disconnects, duplicate delivery, checkpoint recovery, and delayed acknowledgements.
Check recorded operation histories against explicit recovery invariants.
overlap: Useful test-design reference; introducing full Jepsen infrastructure is not justified by source review alone.
risks: Never point Jepsen fault injection at live capital, signing services, or production infrastructure.
A simulated adapter may not capture provider behavior; root-level license was not verified.
validation: Run only against isolated test doubles or deterministic local systems.
Preserve the fault schedule, history, checker result, and exact tested system version.

discoveries: Quint is an executable specification language built on TLA semantics with type checking and developer tooling, aimed at distributed systems and protocols.
The project describes nondeterministic actions, temporal formulas, and a CLI that can find invariant violations in bounded/model runs.
Quint Connect is separately described as model-based testing for Rust; that adapter does not directly test SYLPH TypeScript.
patterns: Specify separation between historical recovery coverage and live-feed health.
Model fail-closed checkpoint validation, queue bounds, and live-tail handoff; retain generated traces.
overlap: Formal model complements TypeScript tests; it does not replace implementation-level verification.
risks: Specification can drift from source behavior; model checking does not certify the compiled Engine.
Bounded exploration and the Rust-specific Connect adapter do not establish all TypeScript executions.
validation: Review state variables against actual implementation fields and transitions.
Convert relevant counterexamples into deterministic TypeScript regression tests and record model bounds.
